definition: How far something can be trusted to work every time.
example: The reliability of the data was questioned.

definition: In a way that can be trusted to happen every time.
example: The train reliably arrives at seven.

definition: The regular journey between home and work.
example: My commute takes about forty minutes each way.

definition: Feeling unable to cope because there is too much to deal with.
example: I felt completely overwhelmed by the number of emails.

definition: A short trip to do a small job, usually for someone else.
example: I have a few errands to run before the shops close.

definition: Easy to understand or do; not complicated.
example: The instructions were straightforward, so it only took ten minutes.

definition: To be grateful for something, or to recognise its value.
example: I really appreciate everything you have done for me.
We split the chores: he cooks and I do the dishes.

definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.
example: The deadline for the report is Monday morning.

definition: To be able to risk doing something without bad consequences.
example: We cannot afford to lose another customer.

definition: To arrange a new time for something.
example: Could we reschedule our call to tomorrow?

definition: To try very hard to do something difficult.
example: He struggled to explain the idea in English.

definition: Good enough to justify the money, time or effort spent.
example: The tickets were expensive, but the concert was worth it.
